title: Climb
subtitle: Cost: 1 extra ft per ft
description: While climbing, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot. This is doubled in difficult terrain.

bullets.content: The DM might require a Strength (Athletics) check for a particularly difficult or sheer surface.

title: Crawl
subtitle: Cost: 1 extra ft per ft
description: While prone, you can crawl. Each foot of movement while crawling costs 1 extra foot.

bullets.content: Crawling is the primary way to move while you are in the Prone condition.

title: Difficult Terrain
subtitle: Cost: 1 extra ft per ft
description: Moving through difficult terrain costs 1 extra foot for every foot of movement.

bullets.content: Examples include dense forests, deep swamps, rubble, or steep stairs.

title: Drop Prone
subtitle: Cost: 0 movement
description: You can drop prone without using any of your speed. This subjects you to the Prone condition.

bullets.content: You cannot be knocked prone again while you are already prone.

title: Grapple Move
subtitle: Move at half speed
description: When you move, you can drag or carry a creature you are grappling, but your speed is halved, unless the creature is two or more sizes smaller than you.

bullets.content: This allows you to reposition a grappled foe on the battlefield.

title: High Jump
subtitle: Leap vertically
description: A high jump allows you to leap into the air. After a 10-foot run-up, you can jump a number of feet equal to 3 + your Strength modifier.

bullets.content: A standing high jump is half that distance. In either case, each foot you clear costs a foot of movement.

title: Improvise
subtitle: Perform an unlisted stunt
description: You can attempt any other kind of movement you can imagine, such as swinging from a chandelier.

bullets.content: The DM tells you whether it is possible and what kind of roll, if any, you need to make.

title: Long Jump
subtitle: Leap across a distance
description: A long jump allows you to leap across a distance. After a 10-foot run-up, you can cover a number of feet up to your Strength score.

bullets.content: A standing long jump is half that distance. In either case, each foot you clear costs a foot of movement.

title: Mount/Dismount
subtitle: Cost: Half your speed
description: Once during your move, you can mount or dismount a creature that is within 5 feet of you.

bullets.content: This costs an amount of movement equal to half your speed. The following rules apply:

items: If an effect moves your mount against its will, you must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity save or fall off, landing prone.
If your mount is knocked prone, you can use your reaction to dismount and land on your feet. Otherwise, you are dismounted and fall prone.

bullets.content: This rule applies to any creature that can serve as a mount.

title: Move
subtitle: Use your speed to move
description: On your turn, you can move a distance up to your speed. You can use as much or as little of your speed as you like on your turn.

bullets.content: The rules for movement are as follows:

items: You can switch between different speeds (e.g., walking and flying) during your move.
You can move through a nonhostile creature's space.
You can move through a hostile creature's space only if it is at least two sizes larger or smaller than you.
Another creature's space is difficult terrain for you.
You can't willingly end your move in another creature's space.

bullets.content: Your movement can be broken up by actions and bonus actions.

title: Stand Up
subtitle: Cost: Half your speed
description: You can stand up from being prone by using an amount of movement equal to half your speed.

bullets.content: You cannot stand up if you don't have enough movement or if your speed is 0.

title: Swim
subtitle: Cost: 1 extra ft per ft
description: While swimming, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot. This is doubled in difficult terrain.

bullets.content: The DM might require a Strength (Athletics) check if you are swimming in rough water.
